newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Two Thai planes land in Phnom Penh to evacuate.
newsitem.headline: Two Thai planes land in Phnom Penh to evacuate.

text.p: Two Thai air force C-130 military transport planes landed at Phnom Penh's battered airport on Tuesday to evacuate Thai and other civilians trapped in Cambodia's fighting, witnesses said.

Thai air force commandos who arrived on the aircraft formed a perimeter around the planes as people ran towards them to try to escape from the city, the scene of factional fighting and turmoil since Saturday.

The first plane took off for Thailand at about 0335 GMT. Thai officials said transport planes would make at least six trips on Tuesday and they expected to take up to 700 people out of the country. The first plane took off for Thailand at about 0335 GMT. Thai officials said transport planes would make at least six trips on Tuesday and they expected to take up to 700 people out of the country. Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said in Bangkok on Tuesday that apart from more than 700 Thai citizens, some 120 Americans, 100 New Zealanders and 300 Pakistanis had also requested to be taken out in the airplanes. He said the first priority was to the Thais but they would try and help others.

The Phnom Penh airport, closed since Saturday, was a scene of devastation after the weekend's fighting and extensive looting on Monday. The airport was stripped of all equipment and ransacked over the three days of violence in the capital and its surroundings.

"I am absolutely happy to get out," said Punnika Srisuanthanch, who was leaving for Bangkok with her 17-year old daughter. The Thais were crammed into mini-busses and pickup trucks and driven through areas which saw heavy fighting on the weekend with burned-out tanks and charred factories lining the main road from the city centre to the airport.
